Report on the Committee's review of the matter sent by the President seeking the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to join the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" and to submit an instrument of accession to the depositary of that Protocol

Report number: M20/R/KG/2026/18
13 October 2026

Foreign Relations Committee

The responsibility of the Foreign Relations Committee is to study matters of foreign relations and, if any change needs to be made to foreign relations policies, to identify it and submit it to the Majlis; and, in relation to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and every office that plans and carries out work related to the foreign sector, to do the things set out in Article 124 (b) to (j) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis.

Accordingly, this includes studying and completing bills submitted by those offices and submitting the Committee's report to the Majlis for its consideration; studying annual reports, identifying matters that need to be rectified and informing them of those matters; studying matters submitted by those offices and advising on how those matters may be taken forward; and meeting those offices, obtaining information and asking questions about the matters they carry out, checking how those offices are doing what they are required to do, and setting out the matters that need to be rectified.

In addition, this also includes studying the relations between the government and the governments of foreign countries, and studying the relations the Maldives maintains with the various international organisations of which the Maldives is a member.

The Committee's responsibilities also include studying treaties and other agreements made by the Maldives with foreign countries and international organisations that are of a kind under which citizens must bear any obligation; studying matters relating to the approval of ambassadors appointed by the Maldives to foreign countries and international organisations; and submitting the Committee's report to the Majlis for its consideration.

1. Introduction

This is the report on the Committee's review of the matter sent by the President, in accordance with Article 115 (k) (1) and Article 93 (a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, seeking the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to join the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" and to submit an instrument of accession to the depositary of that Protocol, at the 3rd sitting of the third session of 2026 of the 20th People's Majlis, held on 7 October 2026.

2. Meetings

At the 25th meeting of this Committee, held on 7 October 2026, the Committee studied the letter sent by the President seeking the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to join the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" and to submit an instrument of accession to the depositary of that Protocol, as well as the information paper and documents prepared by the Ministry of Health, Family and Welfare in relation to that matter. The Committee also decided that the deadline for the Committee to complete its study of that matter would be 13 October 2026.

Thereafter, at the 26th meeting of this Committee, held on 12 October 2026, after the members of the Committee deliberated on the matter, the Committee decided that it was in favour of the Maldives joining that Protocol and submitting an instrument of accession to the depositary of that Protocol.

17. That upon completion of an inquiry, the Committee will send the findings and recommendations of the inquiry to that state, and that the state must respond in writing within 6 (six) months from the date of receiving the Committee's findings and recommendations;

18. That the following are noted as the main reasons for being in favour of approving joining that optional protocol:

• Further demonstrating the importance the Maldives gives to the rights of persons with disabilities: showing that the Maldives has genuine sincerity in protecting the rights of persons with disabilities, and strengthening the commitment made by the Maldivian government to implement the Convention in an appropriate and meaningful manner.

• Strengthening accountability and access to justice: increasing public trust in the accountability of the Maldivian government, as individuals gain an additional opportunity, and as the opportunity to seek additional protection and remedy is facilitated, in circumstances where the remedies available at the national level are insufficient or absent.

• Promoting transparency: showing that the Maldives is open to international review and constructive engagement, and demonstrating that the Maldives will not hesitate to be accountable in international human rights mechanisms.

• Improving the standing of the Maldives in the international arena: paving the way for the Maldives to be seen in the international arena as a country committed to international legal frameworks and respectful of rights, and increasing the credibility and leadership of the Maldives in international human rights forums; and

[stamp] [signature]

23. That the Attorney General's Office has advised that, since this protocol is seen as an international treaty of the kind set out in Article 93 (a) and Article 115 (k) (1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, the Maldives should submit an instrument of accession and join that protocol, in order to become a member of or a party to that protocol, only after completing the procedures set out in the aforementioned articles of the Constitution to be followed when the Maldives joins a treaty;

24. That the Attorney General's Office has advised that, when it is decided that the Maldives will join this protocol, since the procedure set out in Article 93 (a) and Article 115 (k) (1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives to be followed in joining an international treaty must be followed, and since submitting an instrument of accession to accede to that protocol is an agreement to comply with that protocol, the matter of joining the Optional Protocol must, before the instrument of accession is submitted to the depositary of the protocol, be submitted to the People's Majlis for the Majlis to pass and decide on, in accordance with Article 93 (a) of the Constitution; and

25. That the Attorney General's Office has also advised that, once the Majlis passes joining that protocol, it does not see any legal objection to the President signing the instrument of accession that the Maldives must submit in order to join that protocol, and submitting that document to the UN Secretary-General, who has been designated as the depositary of that protocol.

[stamp] [signature]

4. Conclusion

After the Committee studied the matter sent by the President, in accordance with Article 115 (k) (1) and Article 93 (a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, seeking the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to join the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities"

and to submit an instrument of accession to the depositary of that protocol, at the 26th meeting of this Committee, held on 12 October 2026, it was passed by the unanimous agreement of the members present at the Committee and taking part in the vote that the Committee is in favour of the People's Majlis approving the Maldives joining that protocol and submitting an instrument of accession to the depositary of that protocol.

Therefore, we submit this report to the Majlis under Article 124 (j) of the Rules of Procedure of the People's Majlis, requesting that the People's Majlis consider the decision passed by the Committee on the aforementioned matter and decide the matter as the People's Majlis sees fit.

Details of members' attendance at the Committee meetings held to study the matter are given as "Schedule-1" of this report. The matter studied by the Committee is given as "Schedule-2" of this report.

To Honourable Abdul Raheem Abdulla, Speaker of the People's Majlis,

After respectful greetings, I write as follows.

In relation to the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (Optional Protocol), drawn up with the aim of further strengthening matters relating to protecting the rights granted to persons requiring special assistance by the "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities", a treaty ratified by the Maldives on 5 April 2010, fully implementing that Convention, and establishing a system by which member states can be held accountable at the international level, it was decided, after deliberation at the meeting of the Cabinet held on 20 September 2026, that it is seen fit for the Maldives to join that treaty.

Although the aforementioned Optional Protocol is, as set out in Article 115 (p) (1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, an agreement of a kind under which Maldivian citizens are not required to fulfil any obligation as a result of joining that treaty, the matter of international treaties joined by those exercising executive power in the name of the Maldivian State

[stamp] [signature]

must be dealt with by submitting it to the People's Majlis and, after its approval by the Majlis, in accordance with what the Majlis decides, as set out in Article 93 (a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives. Therefore, I request that this matter be submitted to the People's Majlis in order to obtain the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to join the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" and to submit an instrument of accession to the depositary of that protocol, and that I be informed of the decision of the People's Majlis on this matter.

In relation to the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities", a copy of the information paper prepared by the Ministry of Health, Family and Welfare is enclosed with this letter.

Please accept my respects.

Paper submitted to the People's Majlis for a decision on the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities"

1. Title:

On the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities"

2. Matters requiring the approval of the People's Majlis:

Requesting that the People's Majlis approve the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Optional Protocol" or the "Protocol").

3. Executive summary:

It is noted that the Optional Protocol to the "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" is a protocol drawn up with the aim of further strengthening matters relating to protecting the rights granted to persons requiring special assistance by the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (the Convention), ratified by the Maldives on 5 April 2010, fully implementing that Convention, and establishing a system by which member states can be held accountable at the international level. Where a state party to that Convention has taken away from a person or group of persons a right or freedom protected and guaranteed under this Convention, it sets out the procedures for submitting a matter to the "Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities", established under Article 34 of that Convention, establishes a [?] system, and sets out the detailed procedures to be followed in that regard.

[stamp]

4. Background of the matter:

4.1 The "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Convention"), an international human rights treaty, is a treaty that the Maldives ratified and joined on 5 April 2010. The Maldives has not submitted a reservation to any article of that Convention. (A copy of the Convention is included as Schedule 2 of this paper)

4.2 An Optional Protocol setting out a system for submitting complaints to the UN "Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "UN Committee") by or on behalf of a person or group of persons under the jurisdiction of that state, where a right set out in the aforementioned Convention has been lost or taken away, and a system for the UN Committee to conduct inquiries in states, was passed by the UN General Assembly on 13 December 2006. That Optional Protocol came into force on 3 May 2008. (A copy of the Optional Protocol is included as Schedule 1 of this paper)

4.3 Although the Maldives ratified the Convention on 5 April 2010, the Maldives has not joined the Optional Protocol. As a result, at the stage of reviewing the Maldives under various international human rights mechanisms, the Maldives has received many recommendations to ratify this Optional Protocol as soon as possible. (A table of the recommendations received from the various mechanisms is included as Schedule 3 of this paper)

[stamp]

5. Substance of the matter

• This Optional Protocol is a protocol that establishes 2 (two) important mechanisms for strengthening implementation of the Convention by the parties to the Convention.

• The first mechanism is the mechanism for submitting complaints ("individual communications") to the UN Committee by individuals or groups under the jurisdiction of parties that have ratified this protocol, if it is believed that a right of that individual or group set out in the Convention has been lost or taken away, and if those individuals have completed the procedures for seeking all domestic remedies or the legal stages available.

• The second mechanism is the mechanism for the UN Committee to conduct an inquiry in relation to an allegation, if parties that have ratified this protocol are credibly alleged to have violated the rights set out in the Convention in a systematic manner and to a large extent.

• This protocol sets out the conditions for accepting complaints submitted under this protocol, the principles by which complaints will be accepted, and details relating to recommendations made by the UN Committee. In addition, this protocol sets out such things as the procedural protection needed to protect those submitting complaints from retaliation.

Joining the Optional Protocol

• This Optional Protocol is a voluntary protocol. Only parties that ratify and join the protocol are required to comply with the principles of this protocol. Accordingly, out of the 192 (one hundred and ninety-two) parties that have so far joined the Convention, 108 (one hundred and eight) parties have joined this protocol. Therefore,

[stamp]

• The complaint not having evidence supporting it to a reasonable extent, or the matters stated in the complaint being "ill-founded", [?] matters;

• The facts set out in the substance of the complaint having occurred before that party began to comply with this protocol (if the facts continued after it began to comply with the protocol, the complaint may be accepted).

• Article 4 of the Optional Protocol states that when the UN Committee receives a complaint under this mechanism, before a decision is made on the matter of the complaint, the UN Committee may send a request to the party to which the complaint relates asking that party to take measures that must necessarily be taken in order to protect the party who submitted the complaint from irreparable harm that may be caused to it.

• When a complaint is submitted to the UN Committee, the Committee will bring it to the attention of the party to which the complaint relates. And 6 (six) months will be given to respond to the complaint. The Committee will examine the matter in closed meetings, based on all the information submitted to the Committee.

• After examining the complaint, the Committee's views and recommendations will be sent to the member party to which the complaint relates. And the member party to which the complaint relates will be required to respond in writing within 6 (six) months from the date of receiving the Committee's views and recommendations. Article 7 of the Optional Protocol states that, when responding accordingly, it may be asked to share information on any measures taken in relation to the Committee's views and recommendations.

[stamp]

The inquiry mechanism set out in the Optional Protocol

• Under the inquiry mechanism in this protocol, if any member party is credibly alleged to have violated the rights set out in the Convention in a systematic manner and to a large extent, the UN Committee is granted the power to conduct an inquiry in relation to that allegation. Accordingly, Article 6 (5) of the Optional Protocol states that an inquiry conducted must be conducted confidentially, and that the cooperation of the party concerned must be sought at all stages of the entire inquiry.

• If the Committee sees fit during the course of an inquiry, it may visit the party concerned with that party's consent. Upon completion of an inquiry, the Committee will send the results and recommendations of the inquiry to that party. And that party will be required to respond in writing within 6 (six) months from the date of receiving the Committee's results and recommendations.

What is proposed in relation to joining the Optional Protocol

• It is to obtain the approval of the People's Majlis for the Maldives to accede to and join this Optional Protocol. Accordingly, we note the following among the main reasons for being in favour of approving joining this Optional Protocol.

• Further demonstrating the importance the Maldives gives to the rights of persons with disabilities - It shows that the Maldives has a firm commitment to protecting the rights of persons with disabilities. And it strengthens the commitment made by the Maldivian government to implement the Convention in an appropriate and meaningful manner.

[stamp]

• Strengthening accountability and access to justice - Individuals gain an additional opportunity in [?] where there is no remedy at the individual level or [?]. And because the opportunity to seek additional protection and remedy is facilitated, public trust in the accountability of the Maldivian government increases.

• Promoting greater transparency - It shows that the Maldives is open to international review and constructive engagement. And it demonstrates that the Maldives does not hesitate to be accountable to international human rights mechanisms.

• Strengthening the standing of the Maldives in the international arena - It paves the way for the soft power [?] of the Maldives in the international arena as a party committed to international [?] and respectful of rights. And it paves the way for increasing [?] international human rights [?] frameworks and the procedures and practice [?] of the Maldives.

• In addition, we note that these are not mechanisms newly accepted by the Maldives. That is because we note that the Maldives has in this way accepted these same kinds of mechanisms created under other international human rights treaties, and that it is still being held accountable under those mechanisms. Therefore, we note that this work is being carried out by the Attorney General's Office. (Information on other such mechanisms accepted by the Maldives so far is included as Schedule -4 of this paper)

7. Statement of the extent of relation to affected matters

• Impact on the budget:

It is not estimated that the State will incur any additional expense in order to implement this protocol. The reason is that the work of being accountable under other such mechanisms is already work being carried out by the Attorney General's Office. And if the UN Committee visits the Maldives under the inquiry mechanism set out in the protocol, the UN will be responsible for those expenses.

• Legal impact:

It is not considered necessary for a specific law or regulation to come into existence that must be complied with for this protocol once the Maldives ratifies this protocol. The reason is that, while this protocol is a [?] of a treaty, while the opportunity this protocol offers citizens is an additional [?] to submit a matter [?], and while the requirements to be fulfilled in using that mechanism will be determined by the UN Committee, this protocol will not be a treaty of the kind that the Maldives is obliged to act upon, as set out in Article 93 (a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives.

• Impact on human rights:

Setting this out in this protocol will give additional strength to protecting the rights of persons with disabilities. And it will pave the way for implementing the Convention in an appropriate and meaningful manner.

[stamp]

• Section on equalising gender [?] opportunities:

The Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" is not considered to have an adverse impact on gender equality.

• Impact on the environment:

The Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" is not considered to have an adverse impact on the environment.

• Section on publication and providing [?]:

It has not been noted that the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" carries any specific obligation relating to publication and providing [?]

• Need for the public to incur additional expense or do anything:

It is not noted that the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" requires the public to bear additional expense or financial obligation.

8. Proposal submitted on the matter:

To obtain the approval of the People's Majlis that it is seen fit for the Maldives to accede to and join the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities".

To Dr. Aishath Shiham, Minister of Social and Family Development,

After respectful greetings, I write as follows.

With reference to your Ministry's letter number 459-LA/32/2025/23 (14 August 2025), I write since you have requested this Office's advice in relation to the Maldives joining the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Optional Protocol" or the "Protocol").

1. It is noted that the aforementioned Optional Protocol is a protocol drawn up with the aim of further strengthening matters relating to the rights protected for persons requiring special assistance by the "Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Convention"), a treaty ratified by the Maldives on 5 April 2010, and establishing a system by which member states can be held accountable at the international level in fully implementing that Convention; and, accordingly, it is noted that, where a state party to that Convention has taken away from a person or group of persons a right or freedom protected and guaranteed under the aforementioned Convention, it sets out the procedures for submitting a matter to the "Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" (the "Committee"), established under Article 34 of that Convention, establishes a specific system for that, and sets out the detailed procedures to be followed in that regard. Accordingly, it is noted that Article 1 of the Protocol states that states joining the Protocol accept that the Committee has the standing to receive and consider, within the jurisdiction granted to the Committee, a submission made by an individual or group of a member state of the Convention stating that member states of the Convention have violated that Convention.

[stamp]

2. Article 2 of the Optional Protocol sets out the kinds of communications ("matters") that the Committee will not accept. And it is noted that what Article 3 and Article 4 of the Protocol set out are the procedures relating to sharing matters submitted to the Committee with the member state to which the matter relates, how meetings relating to matters so submitted will be conducted, and the procedures relating to informing the member state to which the matter relates and the party that submitted the matter (petitioner) of the matters and recommendations made by the Committee.

3. In addition, considering Article 6 and Article 7 of the Protocol, it is noted that they set out the procedures for how an inquiry will be conducted in relation to a matter if the Committee receives reliable information noting a serious violation, or systematic ongoing violations, by member states contrary to the rights set out in the Convention. And considering Article 8 of the Protocol, it is also noted that it states that, if [a state] does not wish to accept the power granted to the Committee as set out in Articles 6 and 7 as mentioned above, it may declare so when signing or ratifying the Protocol.

4. In addition to the matters noted above in relation to the Protocol, it is noted that the procedure to be followed by states in joining that protocol, the procedure for withdrawing from that protocol, and matters relating to submitting reservations in relation to the Protocol are set out from Article 9 to Article 16 of that protocol. Accordingly;

4.1 Looking at Article 10 of the Protocol, it is noted that the Protocol has been open to states for signature from 30 March 2007. And looking at Article 11 of the Protocol, it is noted that this protocol is a protocol that must be ratified in addition to being signed, and, in addition, it is also noted that the opportunity to 'accede' to the Protocol has been opened to states that have not so far signed the Protocol but have ratified the Convention.

4.2 It is noted that Article 13 of the Protocol states that, after the Convention enters into force, if 10 instruments of ratification or accession are submitted for joining the Protocol, the protocol will enter into force on the date on which 30 days are completed from the date the 10th instrument of ratification or accession is submitted. And where, after 10 instruments of ratification or accession have been submitted as mentioned above, states and regional integration organisations submit an instrument of ratification or accession in ratifying the Protocol, that

[stamp]

protocol will begin to apply to that state or organisation on the date on which 30 days are completed from the date that document is submitted. And accordingly, looking at the information published in relation to the Optional Protocol, it is noted that, since that protocol is a protocol ratified by the required number of states for the protocol instrument, that protocol came into force on 3 May 2008.

4.3 In addition, looking at Article 14 of the Protocol, it is noted that it states that reservations may be submitted on matters that conflict with the object and purpose of that protocol, and that a reservation so submitted may be withdrawn by that state at any time it wishes. And looking at Article 16 of the Protocol, it is noted that it states that if any party that has joined that protocol wishes to withdraw from that protocol, it must notify the UN Secretary-General in writing, and that the party will withdraw from the Protocol upon the completion of 1 (one) year from the date of such written notification.

5. We note the following in relation to the procedures that must be completed under the legal framework of the Maldives when the Maldives joins international treaties.

5.1 Considering Article 93 (a) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives, it states that international treaties must be acted upon by those exercising executive power in the name of the Maldivian State by submitting them to the People's Majlis and, after their approval by the Majlis, in accordance with what the Majlis decides.

5.2 And Article 115 (k) (1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives grants the President the power to sign general agreements, among the treaties and agreements made by the Maldives with foreign countries and international organisations, of the kind under which citizens must bear any obligation.

5.3 Accordingly, since the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities" is seen as an international "treaty" signed between states of the kind set out in Article 93 (a) and Article 115 (k) (1) of the Constitution of the Maldives, in submitting an instrument of accession on behalf of the Maldives in order to become a member of or a party to that protocol, even if joining that protocol, it is in joining a treaty on behalf of the Maldives

[stamp]

only after completing the procedures set out in the aforementioned articles of the Constitution to be followed, we note.

Considering the points set out above, it is our view that, in deciding for the Maldives to join the "Optional Protocol to the Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities", the procedure set out in Article 93 (a) and Article 115 (i) (1) of the Constitution of the Republic of Maldives to be followed in joining an international treaty must be followed; and that, since submitting an instrument of accession to accede to the aforementioned protocol is an agreement to comply with that protocol, the matter of joining the Optional Protocol must, before the instrument of accession is submitted to the depositary of the Protocol, be submitted to the People's Majlis for the Majlis to pass and decide on, in accordance with Article 93 (a) of the Constitution. And accordingly, we advise that once the Majlis passes joining that protocol, we do not see any legal [?] arising when the President signs the instrument of accession that the Maldives must submit in order to join that protocol and submits that document to the UN Secretary-General, who has been designated as the depositary of that protocol.

Yours in sincere service.
